subject: POC entry/exit slate — API keys, org seed, IP allowlist & peering steps
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@cloudhealth.io>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC entry/exit slate — API keys, org seed, IP allowlist & peering steps

Hi Elaine,

Thanks again for the time yesterday — appreciate the deep dive on your latency and data isolation requirements. Per our conversation I've sketched a concise entry/exit slate for the proof-of-concept so we can hit a firm close target. High level ask: if we can complete the items below within the next 7 business days, we can guarantee a fully instrumented POC environment for your team to validate throughput and cost metrics.

Mutual action items (initial):
- CloudHealth: confirm org seed (tenant admin email) and target region for POC (us-west-2 suggested).
- CloudHealth: provide IP allowlist block(s) for API egress (one /24 preferred) and the VPC peer CIDR you want us to peer with.
- CloudHealth: named POC engineer + Security contact (we'll need an SOC evidence owner).
- Redwood: issue ephemeral API keys scoped to POC org & deliver ephemeral key guide (attached).
- Redwood: provision POC tenant and create a dedicated GPU pool (reserved for the test window).

Deliverables Redwood will provide once we receive the above:
- Ephemeral API key bundle and usage/cost dashboard link.
- Time-windowed VPC peering runbook (pre-auth, BGP/route ops not required for peering mode we recommended).
- IP allowlist verification checklist and temporary fallback URL for hosted endpoints.

If that aligns, can you confirm the org admin and security contact by end of day Monday? I attached a short "ephemeral-key guide" and a peering template we typically ask customers to fill out.

Next steps suggested cadence:
- Day 0–2: org seed + IP CIDR + security owner -> Redwood issues keys and schedules peering window.
- Day 3–4: peering + allowlist validation -> smoke tests (tokened workload).
- Day 5–7: performance ramp and acceptance window.

I'm looping Neha for any technical clarifications and Marissa for procurement/questions on the contract timeline.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Logan Wright
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Elaine Park <elaine@cloudhealth.io>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: CloudHealth Security <itsec@cloudhealth.io>
Date: Fri, 30 Jun 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC entry/exit slate — API keys, org seed, IP allowlist & peering steps

Logan — thanks for the clear slate. This looks good and the timeline is ambitious but workable. Quick confirmations:

- Org admin: julia.liao@cloudhealth.io (POC tenant admin)
- Security owner: itsec@cloudhealth.io (I've cc'd them)
- Region: us-west-2 confirmed
- IP allowlist: we'll provide two /28s initially (will send exact CIDRs in a follow-up), and our VPC CIDR is 10.40.0.0/16.

A couple of asks from Security before we proceed:
1) We need to review the ephemeral key lifecycle and rotation policy you mentioned (please include rotation TTL and revocation steps).
2) Peering template — we prefer to pre-authorize a Change Window before any BGP or route updates. Can your peering runbook include a non-BGP peering option?

I'll have the CIDRs and the POC engineer (Benito Ramos) details to you by EOD. If Neha or Marissa need anything else, call out items and we'll prioritize.

—
Elaine Park
Director, Platform Engineering
CloudHealth
elaine@cloudhealth.io | +1 (206) 555-0987

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@cloudhealth.io>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jun 2028 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC entry/exit slate — API keys, org seed, IP allowlist & peering steps

Elaine — perfect, thanks for the quick confirmations. Short responses inline and next actions.

- Ephemeral key lifecycle: TTL default is 24 hours for POC keys; can shorten to 4 hours if you want — keys are revocable from the console immediately. Rotation steps: Redwood issues a new key via our secure token delivery link, old keys become inactive on rotation. We'll attach the lifecycle section in the guide (see attached PDF).
- Peering runbook: yes — we support a VPC-peering mode that does not require BGP or route propagation; we'll include explicit pre-auth change window steps. Our template has both options; we'll mark non-BGP as the recommended option for POC.

Action items (updated):
1) CloudHealth -> send exact CIDRs + Benito Ramos contact (email & phone) by EOD.
2) Redwood -> create POC tenant in us-west-2 and stage ephemeral-key bundle (we'll send the secure delivery link once tenant exists).
3) Redwood -> draft a short day-of-runbook for non-BGP peering and IP allowlist verification; propose an initial 90-minute window for peering ops.

I've started provisioning the tenant under deal CH-2028-0421; Marissa will attach the short SOW addendum for the reserved GPU pool (small example cost table in the doc). Marissa — can you confirm procurement lead time and whether a signed SOW is required before our provisioning?

Thanks,

—
Logan

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>, Elaine Park <elaine@cloudhealth.io>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jun 2028 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC entry/exit slate — API keys, org seed, IP allowlist & peering steps

Hi Elaine / Logan,

Quick procurement note: for standard POC engagements we can start provisioning with a signed mutual-action addendum (one page) plus PO or email approval from CloudHealth procurement. If you prefer a purchase order, our typical lead-time to enable reserved pool is 48 hours after PO receipt. If you sign the one-page addendum and provide an email approval, we can proceed same-day with tenant and keys.

Attached: a draft POC addendum and a small cost table for the reserved GPU pool (this mirrors the brief in the HubSpot deal). If you'd like me to route a DocuSign for the addendum I can do that now — otherwise an email approval from your procurement alias will work for us.

I'll coordinate billing and the SOW link after we get the CIDRs and Benito's contact. Neha, please confirm the scheduled 90-minute peering window works operationally.

Regards,

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Ops
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com

From: Elaine Park <elaine@cloudhealth.io>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: CloudHealth Security <itsec@cloudhealth.io>
Date: Fri, 30 Jun 2028 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC entry/exit slate — API keys, org seed, IP allowlist & peering steps

Thanks all — we will:
- Send exact CIDRs (two /28s) and Benito Ramos contact by 17:00 PT.
- Procurement: will email a PO to marissa.procurement@cloudhealth.io with the one-page addendum attached (please send your DocuSign if easier).
- Security: we reviewed the ephemeral TTL (24h) and prefer a 12h TTL for the acceptance window; can you make that change?

Confirming us-west-2, and we appreciate the non-BGP peering option. Once keys are issued we'll kick off the smoke tests and loop in our infra team.

Elaine
